transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I keep hearing the bank and bill collectors talking about me, like they’re sending me messages that I’ve ruined everything, even when no one else hears anything. It's terrifying because I hear them so clearly, but my wife swears there's no one there.
Along with hearing these voices, have you been feeling extremely sad, down, or hopeless, or lost interest in your usual activities?

Yes, I wake up every day with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, feeling like a complete failure to my wife. I've lost all interest in my gardening and home-brewing, so now I just sit in the garage for hours doing absolutely nothing.
Have you ever heard these voices during times when your mood was completely normal and you weren't feeling depressed, or do they only happen when you are feeling down?

No, I never heard those voices or had those thoughts back when I was working and feeling like myself. They only started after months of feeling deeply depressed, worthless, and completely overwhelmed by our financial worries.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were F32.3, F25, and F20. Based on the patient's confirmation that the auditory hallucinations only occur during periods of deep depression and never when his mood is normal, we can rule out Schizoaffective disorder (F25) and Schizophrenia (F20). This establishes that the psychotic symptoms are entirely mood-congruent and restricted to the depressive episode, pointing definitely to F32.3 (Severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with symptoms of a severe depressive episode, including persistent depressed mood, profound anhedonia, feelings of worthlessness/failure, and psychomotor inactivity. In addition, he experiences mood-congruent auditory hallucinations (voices of bill collectors accusing him of ruining everything) that occur exclusively during the depressive state, confirming a diagnosis of severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3).
